diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exist a compact set $\mathcal{K}\subset \mathbb{C}^d$, with $\mathcal{U} \subset \mathcal{K}$,

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem requires K ⊂ U, whereas the Assumption has U ⊂ K. Since U ⊂ R^d has empty interior in C^d, the stated inclusion would force the interior of K to be empty and make the theorem vacuous. Even with the inclusion corrected, the Assumption only gives U ⊂ K, not U ⊂ interior(K). The claim that the map on the interior of K is a holomorphic extension of f, which is defined on U, needs U ⊂ interior(K). That hypothesis is neither stated nor proved. It is only supplied later, in the corollaries, via E_rho ⊂ interior(K).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the hypothesis as U ⊂ interior(K) (equivalently, assume the interior of K contains U) and correct the inclusion in the theorem. No change to the proof is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 1 as stated is vacuous or does not yield an extension of f. The corollaries add E_rho ⊂ interior(K) and so remain meaningful.
issues.title: Theorem 1 hypothesis on K is reversed and does not guarantee that the map extends f
issues.why_classification: This is a local hypothesis correction. The proof and all downstream uses are unchanged because the corollaries already assume the needed inclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation gives dv/dt ≤ 2 r(M) v ≤ 2 beta v, where v is the squared 2-norm. The proof then drops the factor 2 (dv/dt ≤ beta v, false for M = beta I). Gronwall is then stated with exp(2 ∫ beta). These two steps are inconsistent with each other. Moreover v-tilde(0) equals the squared norm of u_0 and v-tilde(T) is a sup of squared norms. The displayed Gronwall inequality is therefore a bound on squared quantities, but it is declared to correspond to the stated bound on the unsquared norm, with factor ||u_0||_2 rather than ||u_0||_2^2. The sup of a family of differentiable functions, v-tilde, is also differentiated without justification; Gronwall should be applied for each z and the sup taken afterwards. The stated bound (with exp(2 ∫)) is in fact true, since the correct chain gives ||u_0|| exp(∫ beta), but the written proof does not establish it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Gronwall pointwise in z to v = ||u||^2 with v' ≤ 2 beta v, take square roots to get ||u(T,z)|| ≤ ||u_0|| exp(∫ beta), and note that this implies the stated bound.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform bound B is true as stated (it is weaker than what the correct argument gives). Its proof is not valid as written, but later uses of B are unaffected.
issues.title: Step 2 of the Theorem 1 proof: inconsistent factor 2, squared norm confused with norm, supremum differentiated
issues.why_classification: A short routine recomputation fixes the proof and the theorem statement (or a slightly better constant) survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any $f: \mathcal{U} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ that admits a holomorphic extension to a Bernstein polyellipse $\mathcal{E}_{\bm{\rho}} \subset \mathbb{C}^d$

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed approximation term carries a constant C(rho,p) that does not depend on f (nor on d or on the bound B of Theorem 1). For zero noise the LS estimator is linear in f, so replacing f by lambda·f multiplies the left side by lambda while the right side's first term stays fixed. Such a bound cannot hold for all f holomorphic on E_rho, nor for f_v with arbitrarily large B. The cited result is stated for a normalized class (norm at most 1 on the polyellipse), and the adaptation dropped the normalization. The CS bound in the same paper correctly carries ||f||_{L^inf(E_rho)}. The best s-term constants also depend on d, which is likewise omitted. Theorem 1 is supposed to be combined with the cited result to produce B, but B never appears in the LS statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor ||f||_{L^inf(E_rho)} (bounded by B from Theorem 1) and the d-dependence in the constant, e.g. via linearity and rescaling to the normalized class. The noise term stays unchanged. State this in th:main_ls and cor:LS.
issues.overall_effect: The LS error guarantee is misstated, since the dependence on ||f||, hence on B(u_0,T,M), and on d is missing. The rate in m is unaffected.
issues.title: Least-squares bound has constant independent of f (and of d), contradicting linear scaling
issues.why_classification: A scaling argument gives a local statement correction with the same rate and structure, and no new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The data b are scaled by 1/sqrt(m), so the QCBP constraint ||Psi z - b||_2 ≤ eta is in scaled units and requires eta ≥ ||n||_2/sqrt(m). The noise term of Corollary CS is kappa_2·||n||_2/sqrt(m), so the correct replacement is eta itself replacing ||n||_2/sqrt(m). Replacing ||n||_2 by eta gives kappa_2·eta/sqrt(m), which is too small by a factor sqrt(m). For constant adversarial noise n_i = delta, eta ≥ delta, and the replaced noise term ~ delta/sqrt(m) would beat the unavoidable error ≳ delta (data with noise delta·1 are the noise-free data of f + delta). The remark's justification, 'an inspection of its proof reveals', is not carried out. The experiments rely on QCBP, which no proved result covers.

failure_location.quote: up to replacing $\|\bm{n}\|_2$ with the QCBP tuning parameter $\eta$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the QCBP guarantee with eta (assumed at least ||n||_2/sqrt(m)) as the noise term, and cite or verify the corresponding theorem (Theorem 7.4 in the cited book) properly.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed QCBP version of the CS guarantee is misstated, with a noise term that is too optimistic. It also is not actually verified.
issues.title: QCBP extension remark: replacement rule ignores the 1/sqrt(m) scaling and gives an impossible noise term
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction to a remark's scaling. The main corollaries are for SR-LASSO and are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: be either the uniform or Chebyschev measure on $\mathcal{U}=[-1,1]^d$
To prove the theorem it is enough to apply \cite[Theorem 6.1]{adcock2022monte} combined with \cite[Remark 5.2]{adcock2022monte}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof computes coefficients with Lebesgue measure dx and claims the one-dimensional factor vanishes. Orthonormal polynomials are orthogonal to constants only with respect to their own measure. For the Chebyshev measure, with Chebyshev polynomials the integral against dx does not vanish (for nu_k = 2 it equals -2/3 up to normalization), so the displayed step is false in a case the theorem explicitly covers. The proof also never verifies that a function of the first d variables meets the hypotheses of the infinite-dimensional cited theorem, which is stated for a different holomorphy class, and p is left undefined in the statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the vanishing-coefficient computation with the product measure rho (orthogonality to psi_0 under rho), and state the hypotheses of the cited theorem and p explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The support-reduction argument is valid as written only for the uniform/Legendre case. The Chebyshev case of th:main_ls and cor:LS is not established as written.
issues.title: Proof of finite-dimensional LS theorem integrates against Lebesgue measure; fails for the Chebyshev measure; hypotheses of the cited theorem not checked
issues.why_classification: The fix is a routine local change of measure in the same computation, and the conclusion is unchanged.
